nodes.description: In neonatal mice MAB21L1 is expressed in two mesenchymal populations of the external genitalia, beneath the scrotal and labial skin and around the preputial and clitoral glands. Mab21l1-null pups have a smaller scrotum, vulva and preputial and clitoral glands, with reduced mesenchymal cell density, proliferation and extracellular matrix. The preputial gland is a rodent derivative of the cranial scrotal fold, so this models the absent labioscrotal folds of patients.

nodes.description: In the mouse lens placode, Mab21l1 acts downstream of PAX6. Its loss reduces Foxe3 expression and, at single-cell resolution, alters 279 genes, including the lens-formation genes Pitx3, Maf and Sfrp2 and housekeeping genes of DNA and nucleotide metabolism, before the cells die. The authors propose that MAB21L1 acts as a nuclear factor modulating these programmes.

nodes.description: Homozygous frameshift and nonsense variants, plus one missense variant (p.Gln233Pro) predicted to disrupt an alpha helix, are expected to abolish MAB21L1 function. MAB21L1 has the nucleotidyltransferase fold of cGAS, but no nucleotidyltransferase activity has been demonstrated, so the lost function is thought to be non-catalytic; the protein associates with the PAX6 regulators MEIS1, MEIS2 and PBX1. Loss of these interactions in patients is proposed but has not been measured. All coding variants lie in the single coding exon.

The step from the mouse lens defect to the human corneal phenotype is inferred.
